findings.title: Cart total test asserts against opaque magic number
findings.note: Assertion is a bare literal (2000) with no derivation from the unit price or quantity used in the test, so a reader cannot tell if the expectation is correct without cross-referencing pricing.ts separately.

findings.title: Skipped bulk-pricing test asserts a value inconsistent with current price table
findings.note: Test is disabled (it.skip) and never runs in CI; its magic-number expectation (900) does not match the current PRICES table (A1: 1000) in pricing.ts, so bulk pricing is untested and the skip masks that no such logic exists in priceOf.

findings.title: CI wraps the whole test run in a 3-attempt retry

evidence.quote:
- uses: nick-fields/retry@7152eba30c6575329ac0576536151aca5a72780e
        with:
          timeout_minutes: 10
          max_attempts: 3
          command: npm test

findings.note: The entire npm test invocation, not an individual flaky test, is retried up to 3 times; this configuration would silently absorb any non-deterministic test failure without surfacing it, though no flaky-commit history was available to confirm one exists.

looks_bad_but_fine.why: expect(priceOf("nope")).toBe(0) asserts a literal 0 but this is the documented default/fallback value, not an opaque magic number, so it is fine.

not_assessed: Whether the CI retry configuration is currently masking a known flaky test (no flaky-commit history available)
